The pinned newline exception and no-trailing-bytes requirement leave framing unclear, while both reference parsers trim whitespace; bounded framing vectors should use the existing unparseable_stdout classification rather than stdout_malformed.

Sections 7.3 and 8 already specify insertion of entry.nonce without operator namespacing, leaving narrower coverage gaps while duplicate-as-schema-invalid and nonce_replayed expectations introduce unsupported schema and harness semantics.

Deadline scope and request-write failure handling merit clarification, although both pinned reference hosts already avoid blocking on stdin delivery and the runner supports request_raw for a large-request fixture.

Cross-issuer replay coverage is absent, but nonce-only reservation is already specified and both reference stores implement that key, while the proposed shared-store two-run test requires runner support beyond a fixture pair.

The pinned schema and prose permit already-elapsed retention timestamps without a host check, supporting bounded defensive validation and vectors, although neither reference store demonstrates immediate eviction and a compromised verifier remains trusted to decide authorization.

Both pinned hosts condition reservation on host mode, and Rust explicitly tests ignoring consume_nonces locally, confirming a concrete configuration-mismatch hazard addressable by requiring reservation or explicit denial.

Atomic insertion is already required by §7.3, but the sequential runner and reference read-modify-write stores leave concurrency untested; adding parallel alone cannot implement or reliably expose the race.

Section 9 already permits invalid_proof for failed token checks and §3.3 provides detail for precise internal reasons, supporting at most a revocation-mapping clarification rather than a missing representable denial outcome.

The pinned secrecy prohibition covers message but omits detail despite its designated logging role, making a matching prohibition and non-authorization clarification useful without changing the verdict schema.

An agent_name string can already identify an instance, so the six-field binding does not imply necessarily shared bindings, and prescribing class identity would introduce an unsupported semantic restriction.

Receipt chaining exists in the pinned source, but AuthReceiptInput requires substantial identity and proof context absent from an EVC verdict, and the proposal lacks a concrete mapping, complete package pins, and executable receipt-generation commands.
At 9bf7544 Appendix B is already explicitly informative, excludes EVC conformance obligations, uses lowercase must, and defines serialization without the alleged npm dependency.

The pinned IANA section already specifies Specification Required, version-qualified registration and initial contents, explicitly reconciles the closed enum, and separately explains why kind receives no registry.

The pinned historical 27/27 listing and current 29-vector suite establish a useful rerun opportunity for [RFC 7942 coverage reporting](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7942#section-2), with actual results and a resolved host command required and no contact with the held maintainer.

Official [ExtMCP documentation](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/kubernetes/1.3.x/documentation/mcp/guardrails/about/) confirms pre-forward external decisions through an existing gRPC protocol, supporting possible composition while leaving subprocess integration and maintainer interest unverified.

Both pinned hosts and the empty ledger support fresh run records, but reproduction needs --type host_behavior, the exact Rust binary, preserved runner exit status, isolated scratch execution, and observed results rather than presumed 29/29 passes.

Local sync:check passes, but matching PASS-line IDs cannot establish published fixture or expectation parity, and the repository command omits host-only filtering while its pipeline discards the runner exit status.

The external commit and historical coverage are verified in the pinned draft, supporting a current rerun consolidated with the overlapping RFC7942 candidate, while failures must remain run evidence rather than automatically count as passing implementations or specification regressions.

An explicit map would improve the existing scoring heuristic, but section-citation joins do not demonstrate clause coverage, fixture descriptions reside in test-vectors.json, and existing positive controls and PID assertions already test EOF and killing.
